what: With the panel pinned for 2 screens, a screen-wide curtain tied to scroll moves in 21 stepped jumps (steps) from off the left to off the right (−100% → 133.3%), and the character pulling the curtain’s left edge sways 10°·−10° each step. After the 9th step, when the curtain covers the whole screen, the section given hide is hidden so the scene behind the curtain changes (shown again on rewind) and fx:step fires — a closing curtain you drag by hand to switch scenes, like a stage curtain

options.to: End position (xPercent), default 133.333 — even the leftmost character leaves the screen
options.at: Cells fully covered, default computed from to (9 for 21 cells)
options.hide: Selector for the sheet to hide after the full-cover cell passes
options.swings: Number of shake steps, default steps (original phone 14)
options.scrub: true (default, bound immediately) or seconds to follow late
options.priority: refreshPriority, default 0 — use a smaller value if it must be measured after the previous section’s pin
options.[data-fx-part=puller]: Character that dismisses the curtain (child, if any)

from.where: index.html .sm-curtain — the page-end #curtain (margin −300vh) is pinned for 2 screens from bottom bottom, an olive, orange and maroon striped curtain passes in steps(21), and at the 9th cell #epilogue is hidden so the pinned Hero is revealed

note: The original changes hiding only when it passes exactly one of the 9 cells at a time — the part decides by whether it has passed at, so it still changes when fast scrolling skips cells. Sending the page back to the top after the end is up to the consumer (the original calls scrollTo(0,0) at 10px from the document end).
